en: The Analysis of the Bhikkhunī Rules,

2.12 Chapter on the Modes of Comprehension (Saṅgahavāra) Regarding the offenses committed by reason of consenting to physical contact: by how many of the seven classes of offenses are these offenses comprised?
The offenses committed by reason of consenting to physical contact are comprised of five of the seven classes of offenses.

They may belong to the class of offenses involving defeat (pārājika), they may belong to the class of offenses involving formal meeting of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa), they may belong to the class of grave offenses (thullaccaya), they may belong to the class of offenses requiring expiation (pācittiya), or they may belong to the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) … [and so on] … By how many of the seven classes of offenses are the offenses incurred by reason of requesting and eating curd included among the seven classes of offenses?

The offenses incurred by reason of requesting and eating curd are included in two of the seven classes of offenses: [namely, the class of offenses involving formal meeting of the Saṅgha and the class of offenses requiring expiation].
It may be by way of the class of offenses entailing confession (pāṭidesanīya), or it may be by way of the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
The fourth section on inclusion is finished.
